steps: Open a new chat in the web app.
Type any short question in the composer.
Press the Send message button.
Look for the Preparing line with the spinning mark under your message, before any answer text appears.
S19.01.where: Composer: type a message and press Send message; the chat then shows Preparing before the answer

S19.02.note: A separate Queued row also exists in ChatComposerNew.tsx; which one shows depends on composer state, not verified in the running app.
steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
While it is still answering, type a second message in the composer.
Press Send message.
Look for the Queued chip next to the send button (with a count if more than one is queued).
S19.02.where: Composer: send a second message while the first reply is still running; a Queued chip appears beside the send button

S19.03.note: No separate wording for reading context, attachments or memory was found; the only visible word is Preparing.
steps: Open a new chat.
Attach a file with the attachment control in the composer.
Type a question about the file and press Send message.
Look for Preparing while the file is read, before the answer starts.
S19.03.where: Composer: send a message with an attachment; the chat shows Preparing before the model answers

S19.04.needs: a turn that uses web search
steps: Send a question that needs current information from the web.
Look at the activity timeline above the answer while it runs.
Look for Searching the web, followed by the search summary if one is shown.
S19.04.where: Composer: send a question that needs web search; the activity timeline shows Searching the web

S19.05.needs: a model route that runs code
steps: Ask the model to calculate something by running Python code.
Look for the code execution block in the answer.
Look for Running Python while the step is executing, then the Output section when it finishes.
S19.05.where: Composer: ask the model to run Python code; the code block shows Running Python while it runs

S19.06.note: The connector sentence is built from the summary text; the exact settings path to connect a service was not traced.
steps: Connect a service in the app's connectors settings, then open a new chat.
Ask for something that needs that service.
Look at the activity timeline for a step that names the service with Using.
Check that the step shows the call in progress until it finishes.
S19.06.where: Composer: send a request that uses a connected connector; the activity step names the connector with Using

S19.07.needs: a tool that asks for approval
S19.07.note: The exact approve and deny button words were not found by search; the tester should read them on screen.
steps: Send a request that triggers a tool needing approval.
Look for the Needs approval label in the activity timeline.
Look for the note Waiting for approval. This response is partial; review the tool request to continue.
Check that approve and deny controls appear on the tool step.
S19.07.where: Composer: send a request that needs approval for a tool step; the turn shows Needs approval

S19.08.needs: a task that makes the assistant ask a question
S19.08.note: The answer control's exact visible words were not checked.
steps: Send a task that is vague, so the assistant needs a detail from you.
Look for the Waiting for your input label in the activity timeline.
Find the question card in the answer and type a reply into it.
Check that the turn continues after you reply.
S19.08.where: Composer: send a task where the assistant asks a question mid-task; the activity shows Waiting for your input

steps: Send a question in a new chat.
Watch the Generating response line under your message.
As soon as the first words appear, check that the Generating response line is gone and the answer text is shown.
S19.09.where: Shown in the chat thread when the first answer text arrives; the Generating response line gives way to the answer

steps: Open a new chat and type a question that gives a longer answer.
Press Send message.
Watch the answer grow in the chat thread while it is still running.
Check that the text grows in pieces, not all at once when the answer finishes.
S19.10.where: Composer: send any question; the answer text appears word by word in the chat thread

steps: Send a request such as Make a table of three fruits with their colours, or Write a short Python function.
Watch the answer while it is still streaming.
Check that the table, list or code block is drawn correctly before the answer finishes.
Check that the finished answer shows the same structure.
S19.11.where: Composer: ask for a list, a table or a code block; check it while the answer is still streaming

steps: Ask the assistant to create a document or a small file.
Look at the artifact row in the answer while it is being made.
Look for the word Creating and the Show the code being written action.
Check that the row changes to Created a file when it is done.
S19.12.where: Composer: ask for a file or document; the chat shows Creating while it is built, then Created a file

S19.13.needs: a model route that generates images
S19.13.note: The generating text on the media card was not found by search; the progress UI is in MessageBubble.tsx around the media card.
steps: Ask the assistant to generate an image of a simple object.
Look at the media card in the answer while it generates.
Check that a progress or generating state is shown before the picture appears.
S19.13.where: Composer: ask for an image or a video; the media card shows generation progress

S19.15.note: Response complete is a status string for assistive tech and was not seen as a visible label; a visible completed label was not found.
steps: Send a short question and wait for the answer to finish.
Check that the Generating response line and the Preparing line are gone.
Check that the answer is marked complete for screen readers, for example with the Response complete announcement.
S19.15.where: Chat thread: a finished turn shows no loading line and its state is named for screen readers

S19.16.needs: a multi-step turn where one step fails
S19.16.note: No visible label Partially completed was found in the code.
steps: Send a request that uses several steps, such as a search plus a tool call.
Let one step fail, or wait for a run where a step fails.
Look for Finished with errors in the activity timeline or the Response finished with errors line under the answer.
Check that it is not shown as Response complete or Response failed.
S19.16.where: Chat thread or activity timeline: a run with some failed steps shows Finished with errors

steps: Send a question that gives a long answer.
Press the stop button in the composer (its tooltip says Stop generation).
Look for the Stopping the Cloud task line in the answer, below the text.
Check that the line stays until the run has stopped.
S19.17.where: Composer: while an answer is running, press Stop generation; the chat shows Stopping the Cloud task

steps: Send a long question and press Stop generation partway.
Check that the text that arrived is still shown above.
Look for the line Response stopped. with a Try again button.
Look for Response cancelled. Partial response saved. in the message status if shown.
S19.18.where: Chat thread: after Stop, the answer keeps the text that arrived and shows Response stopped. with Try again

S19.19.needs: a way to drop the network connection
steps: Send a long question.
Turn off Wi-Fi on the Mac while the answer is running.
Look for the Reconnecting… line under the answer.
Turn Wi-Fi back on and check whether the answer continues.
S19.19.where: Chat thread: if the network drops during a turn, the line Reconnecting... shows until it resumes

S19.20.needs: a turn that is still running when the tab is closed
S19.20.note: No visible Resuming word was found; the effect is seen only through the answer continuing.
steps: Send a long question in a chat.
Close the browser tab while the answer is still running.
Open the same chat again from the sidebar.
Check that the answer continues from where it was, and that the text does not start again from the top.
S19.20.where: Shown by reopening a chat while a reply is running; the answer carries on instead of starting again

labels.text: This model is receiving too many requests right now.

S19.21.needs: a provider rate limit, which is hard to make happen on demand
steps: Send a message to a model that is receiving too many requests.
Look for the notice under the reply.
Check that it says to wait and retry, and names another model if your plan has one.
S19.21.where: Chat thread: a rate-limited turn shows the rate-limit notice under the failed reply, with Retry

labels.text: You have reached a usage limit on your account.

S19.22.needs: an account at its usage limit
S19.22.note: The Usage screen location was not traced in the menus.
steps: Use an account that has reached its usage limit.
Send a message.
Look for the notice: You have reached a usage limit on your account.
Check that it points to Usage to see when it resets.
S19.22.where: Chat thread: a turn blocked by an account usage limit shows the usage notice with Usage

labels.text: Your session ended before this turn finished. Sign in again, then retry.

S19.23.note: The code has the words Sign in again in the notice text, but no sign-in button tied to it was found.
steps: Let the session expire, or sign out in another tab, then send a message.
Look for the notice: Your session ended before this turn finished.
Check whether a Sign in again control is offered next to the notice.
S19.23.where: Chat thread: a turn that fails because sign-in expired shows the session notice

S19.24.needs: the desktop app linked and then offline
steps: Start a task that needs the desktop app, with the desktop app closed.
Look at the activity timeline in the chat.
Look for Waiting for your desktop, with the device name if one is shown.
S19.24.where: Activity timeline: when a step needs your desktop and it is offline, the step shows Waiting for your desktop

labels.text: The model provider is temporarily unreachable.

S19.25.needs: a provider outage, or a free route that is overloaded
steps: Send a message to a model whose provider is down or overloaded.
Look for the notice under the reply.
Check that it says the provider is temporarily unreachable and offers Retry or another model.
S19.25.where: Chat thread: when the model provider is unavailable the notice offers Retry or another model

labels.text: This message is too long for the selected model.

S19.26.needs: a very long message or an unsupported attachment
S19.26.note: Failed-turn text restore was reported in an earlier run, not checked here.
steps: Paste a very long message, or attach a file the model cannot read.
Send it.
Look for the notice that names the problem, such as This message is too long for the selected model.
Check that the text is put back in the composer so you can fix and resend.
S19.26.where: Chat thread: a message that is too long or an attachment the model cannot read shows the fix to make, with Retry

labels.text: The part that arrived is kept above.

S19.27.needs: a way to make the provider fail mid-answer (no reliable on-demand trigger found in the code); a Free account can reach the fallback route
S19.27.note: The failure text comes from the stream_interrupted error code (apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts line 149 and apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/upstream-error-copy.ts line 101); the exact trigger is not reachable on demand, and the English text is also in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx line 117 as a lookup.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat from the first screen.
Send a long request, such as "Write a detailed 2000-word guide", so the answer runs for a while.
Wait for the connection or provider to fail while text is still arriving (this is not something a tester can force on demand; if it does not happen, mark it unsure).
Check that the text that already arrived stays on the page, and that the message says the response stopped part way through and the part that arrived is kept above.
Check that a "Retry" button is offered, and that the failed state is shown in the turn's activity details.
S19.27.where: Chat > send a message > the answer stops part way through > look for the "Retry" button under the failed turn

S19.28.needs: a signed-in account that can produce a failed or stopped turn
S19.28.note: The restore path was located in code (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx and the messages persist route) but the exact sidebar section shown on the web app was not confirmed visually; the label Recents is from the shared locale file.
steps: Start a chat and let one turn finish as failed (for example a provider error) or stop it with the stop control.
Note the turn's final state: the failure text, or the stopped state.
Quit the app completely and open it again, then sign in if asked.
Find the same conversation under Recents in the sidebar and open it.
Compare the conversation and that turn's final state (failed or stopped) with what you noted before the restart.
S19.28.where: Sidebar > Recents > open a conversation that ended as failed or stopped, after quitting and reopening the app

S19.29.needs: a signed-in account; desktop notification permission for the notification part
S19.29.note: This is server-side behaviour in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts (durable run start near line 642) with the resume logic in apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts near line 3118; whether the run keeps going after a tab closes was not confirmed by reading the code alone.
steps: Start a long answer in a chat.
Close the browser tab or window while the answer is still generating.
Wait a minute or two, then open the app or the same conversation again from Recents.
Check that the answer is complete or still being produced, and that a desktop notification titled "Your reply is ready" appeared when the app was in the background.
S19.29.where: No control; its effect is seen in the conversation after reopening, and as a desktop notification when the reply is ready
